sentences.text: Many decisions are thought to arise via the accumulation of noisy evidence to a threshold or bound, which determines choice, reaction time, and confidence through a decision variable.
In perception, stimulus strength, measured by signal-to-noise ratio, affects decision speed, accuracy, and confidence through this accumulation process.
An increase in noise is predicted to cause faster decisions, reduced accuracy, and paradoxically higher confidence, especially when the momentary evidence is weak.
The study introduced a novel sensory manipulation that added unbiased noise to motion-selective regions of the visual cortex, verified by neuronal recordings from macaque areas MT and MST.
This manipulation increased the volatility of motion information in a random dot motion display without changing the average motion strength or direction.
For both humans and monkeys, increasing noise caused faster decisions and greater confidence across a range of stimuli, while accuracy was only minimally impaired.
The magnitude of these effects on decision speed and confidence matched the predictions of a bounded evidence accumulation model that accounts for motion strength and volatility.

sentences.text: The deamidase OspI from the bacterium Shigella flexneri changes a glutamine amino acid at position 100 in the host enzyme UBC13 into glutamate, a process called deamidation.
This deamidation at Q100 stops UBC13 from working with the RING-finger ubiquitin ligase TRAF6 to add polyubiquitin chains, which silences the NF-κB inflammatory response.
Deamidation weakens the interaction between UBC13 and the TRAF6 RING domain by disturbing both their stable (native) and temporary (transient) contacts.
This weakening happens without changing the overall shape or enzymatic activity of UBC13.
Deamidation creates a new internal salt-bridge between R14 and E100 in UBC13 that competes with an important salt-bridge between R14 in UBC13 and E69 in TRAF6RING, reducing their binding.
The competition between these salt-bridges lowers the stability of the UBC13/TRAF6RING complex.
Salt-bridge competition and electrostatic repulsion reduce transient interactions needed to form the UBC13/RING complex, lowering how fast and how stably they associate.
The negative charge of E100 in deamidated UBC13 repels the negatively charged surface of the TRAF6 RING domain, further preventing transient interactions.
This study shows that the post-translational modification deamidation changes the shape and stability of transient UBC13/RING complexes to inhibit their protein-protein association.

sentences.text: Working memory is supported by coordinated interactions among large-scale distributed brain networks, particularly involving frontal and parietal brain regions.
Oscillatory synchronization, especially in the theta frequency range (around 4 to 6 Hz), is thought to enable information exchange within and between brain networks during working memory tasks.

Theta (6 Hz) transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) was applied to the middle frontal gyrus and inferior parietal lobule nodes of the right frontoparietal network in synchronous (0° relative phase) and desynchronous (180° relative phase) conditions.
Applying synchronous theta-frequency tACS to the right frontoparietal network improved working memory performance when cognitive demands were high.
The effects of tACS on brain activity depended on the relative phase of stimulation and the internal cognitive processing state, as shown by simultaneous fMRI data.
During a verbal working memory task, synchronous tACS increased parietal brain activity, which correlated with better behavioral performance.
Functional connectivity results showed that the relative phase of frontoparietal stimulation influenced information flow within the working memory network.
Overall, the study found a direct link between behavioral performance in a demanding working memory task and large-scale brain synchronization across a right frontoparietal network.

sentences.text: The granular retrosplenial cortex (RSG) is critical for both spatial and non-spatial behaviors.

Researchers used channelrhodopsin-assisted circuit mapping (CRACM) in mice to study subtype-specific circuits formed by anterior thalamic, claustral, anterior cingulate, and dorsal subicular inputs to the RSG.
The anterior thalamus and dorsal subiculum, which provide spatial information, strongly and selectively recruit small low-rheobase (LR) pyramidal cells in the RSG.
In contrast, neighboring regular-spiking (RS) cells are preferentially controlled by claustral and anterior cingulate inputs, which carry mostly non-spatial information.
Precise sublaminar axonal and dendritic arborization within layer 1 of the RSG allows parallel processing of spatial and non-spatial inputs.
Thalamocortical synaptic dynamics enable LR neurons in the RSG to compute the speed of head rotation, even though the head direction inputs they receive do not explicitly encode speed.
These parallel input streams identify LR neurons as a distinct principal neuronal subtype ideally positioned to support spatial orientation computations in the RSG.

sentences.text: Petal number is invariant in Arabidopsis thaliana flowers but varies in the closely related species Cardamine hirsuta, and the genetic basis for this difference is unknown.
Cardamine hirsuta shows variation in petal number, with flowers producing between zero and four petals across 39 natural accessions sampled from across the species range.
Divergence in the floral regulator APETALA1 (AP1) can account for the species-specific difference in petal number robustness between Arabidopsis thaliana and Cardamine hirsuta.

Arabidopsis thaliana AP1 confers robustness in petal number by masking the phenotypic expression of quantitative trait loci controlling petal number in Cardamine hirsuta through epistatic interactions.

Cardamine hirsuta AP1 fails to complement the robustness function of Arabidopsis thaliana AP1, resulting in variable petal number, and upstream regulatory regions of AP1 contribute to this divergence.
Variable petal number is maintained in Cardamine hirsuta despite sufficient standing genetic variation in natural accessions to produce plants with four-petalled flowers.

sentences.text: Some viruses like Marburg virus, Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV), and Dengue virus activate and benefit from the protein Nrf2, but Nrf2 mobilization counters HIV infection in macrophages.
Before this study, the impact of Nrf2 activation on HIV infection had not been tested.
Sulforaphane (SFN), a compound produced in cruciferous vegetables after damage, activates Nrf2 and changes gene expression strongly.
SFN blocks HIV infection in primary macrophages but does not block infection in primary T cells.
SFN also blocks HIV infection in PMA-differentiated promonocytic cell lines but not in other tested cell lines.
Reducing Nrf2 levels with siRNA increases HIV infection in primary macrophages and lowers the antiviral effect of SFN.
SFN blocks HIV infection after the virus enters cells but before the formation of 2-LTR circles, similar to the antiviral proteins SAMHD1 and MX2.
SFN does not increase the levels of the antiviral proteins SAMHD1 or MX2 during HIV infection inhibition.
This study shows for the first time that activating Nrf2 can strongly block HIV infection and reveals a new way to trigger antiviral inhibition.

sentences.text: The Dominican Republic experienced a large dengue epidemic followed closely by Zika virus cases, providing an opportunity to study differences in transmission between these two flaviviruses.
Seventy-five percent of dengue cases occurred in people younger than 20 years, while Zika infections were more evenly distributed across age groups.
Dengue attack rates were marginally higher among males at 25.9 per 10,000 population compared to 21.5 per 10,000 population for females.
Zika infections were highly clustered among females, accounting for 73.8% of cases, with age-adjusted attack rates of 7.64 per 10,000 population in females versus 2.72 per 10,000 in males.
The basic reproduction number (R0) for Zika was higher in females at 1.84 compared to 1.72 in males.
Guillain-Barre syndrome (GBS) attack rates were slightly higher in males at 0.62 per 10,000 population compared to 0.57 per 10,000 in females.
Existing dengue immunity appears to have little impact on the population-level attack rates of Zika virus.
Community awareness campaigns likely increased health-seeking behaviour and reporting among women of reproductive age during the Zika outbreak, though biological susceptibility cannot be ruled out.

sentences.text: Under nitrogen deprivation, filaments of the cyanobacterium Anabaena develop a one-dimensional pattern of nitrogen-fixing heterocysts separated by about ten photosynthetic vegetative cells.

The transcription factor HetR is essential for heterocyst differentiation in Anabaena, and its gene expression fluctuations were studied using a chromosomally-encoded translational hetR-gfp fusion under both nitrogen-rich and nitrogen-deprived conditions.
Statistical analysis shows that hetR expression fluctuations in nearby cells along Anabaena filaments are coupled with a spatial range of about two to three cells.
These correlations between cells mainly arise from intercellular molecular transfer and less from cell division, as correlations persist in septal protein mutants.

Fluctuations in hetR expression under nitrogen-rich conditions form clusters that are statistically similar to early times after nitrogen deprivation and later resolve into single heterocysts through lateral inhibition.

Under nitrogen-rich conditions, basal expression of the HetR inhibitor PatS, cell-cell communication influenced by the septal protein SepJ, and positive HetR auto-regulation determine hetR expression fluctuations and their distribution along filaments.

Comparison of hetR-gfp expression under nitrogen-rich and nitrogen-poor conditions highlights differences between the HetR inhibitors PatS and HetN, and differences in specificity between the septal proteins SepJ and FraC/FraD.

Proteins involved in activation, inhibition, and cell-cell communication combine with stochasticity in gene expression to control coupled fluctuations that produce the one-dimensional developmental pattern in Anabaena filaments.

sentences.text: Humans can learn and store multiple visuomotor mappings when feedback for each is provided alternately, a process called dual-adaptation.
Learned context cues associated with each visuomotor mapping can be used to switch between the stored mappings without feedback.
Little is known about how associative learning between contextual cues and visuomotor mappings generalises to novel but similar conditions.
Participants performed a rapid target-pointing task on a graphics tablet with manipulated visual feedback to simulate different visuomotor mappings based on target shapes.
After training, participants were tested without feedback on novel target shapes that had not been learned previously to assess generalisation.
The study compared two hypotheses: an explicit linear generalisation model and an implicit Bayesian learning model predicting categorisation-like generalisation.

Experimental results show that participants, who had explicit awareness of the cues’ role, applied the mapping corresponding to the trained shape most similar to the current one, consistent with the Bayesian learning model.
The Bayesian learning model predicts that learning slows down with increased numbers of training pairs, which was confirmed by the experimental results.
Overall, the Bayesian learning model provides a possible mechanism for simultaneously learning multiple visuomotor mappings.

sentences.text: Currently, each neglected tropical disease (NTD) program has its own mapping methodology, and conducting multiple surveys in the same country can be costly and burdensome to national disease programs.
Because NTDs tend to overlap geographically, an integrated approach to mapping NTDs might result in more efficient identification of populations needing treatment.

We developed and field-tested an innovative integrated NTD mapping protocol called Integrated Threshold Mapping (ITM) Methodology for lymphatic filariasis, trachoma, schistosomiasis, and soil-transmitted helminths.
The ITM protocol is designed to be resource-efficient and aims to determine whether a threshold to trigger public health interventions in an implementation unit has been reached.

The protocol uses World Health Organization (WHO) recommended indicators in disease-specific age groups, with the district as the sampling frame for each disease except schistosomiasis, which uses the sub-district.
We tested the ITM methodology by comparing it to current WHO mapping methodologies in one district each in Mali and Senegal.

The ITM methodology reached the same conclusions as the WHO methodologies regarding public health interventions for trachoma, lymphatic filariasis, and soil-transmitted helminths, but resulted in more targeted intervention recommendations for schistosomiasis.
The ITM methodology was practical, feasible, and demonstrated overall cost savings compared with the standard, non-integrated WHO methodologies.
This integrated mapping tool could facilitate the implementation of much-needed NTD programs in endemic countries.
